opennyai_summary.4_October_2024__facts:
The accused in S.C.No.506 of 2018 on the files of the Special Court for the trial of offences under the PoCSO Act, Kottayam is the appellant.
He is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.50,000/- each under Section 376(2)(i),

opennyai_summary.4_October_2024__ANALYSIS:
While filing the final report, the dates of incidents were corrected as 16.05.2017 and 17.05.2017.
If those were the actual dates of occurrence, there was absolutely no probability for PW1 connecting the dates with Onam, especially when she gave Ext.P1 statement on 31.07.2017, which was not a far distant date.
But when only evidence that could be used 2024:KER:73889 to prove the charge is that of PW1, the victim, such inconsistencies cannot fully be overlooked.
15. Considering the nature of the alleged incident, the possibility of having any serious injury suggestive of such a sexual assault is remote.
PW5 did not notice any injuries and found hymen of PW1 intact.
Thus, there is no medical evidence to support the case of the prosecution.
The history of sexual assault by the appellant was stated to PW5.
In the absence of any clinical indication suggestive of such a sexual assault, the statement of PW1 to PW5 regarding the sexual assault, which was given after such a distance of time, can be treated only as a hearsay information.
Therefore, the evidence of PW5 is not available to corroborate the version of PW1 in court.
16. The evidence thus, the prosecution can rely on is the oral testimony of PW1.
When PW2 and PW4 did not state 2024:KER:73889 anything before the court, which may amount to a res gestae or give any corroborative statement, oral testimony of PW1 stands proved.
17. PWs.1 and 2 admitted that PW2 and her sister who is the wife of the appellant were not in good terms; not even in talking terms.
When the evidence of PW1 is considered in that context, the same cannot be acted upon to prove the basic facts enabling to draw the presumption under Section 29 of the PoCSO Act.
The proposition of law is trite that the evidence of the victim is sufficient to enter a conviction in a charge of rape.
But the court should be able to trust the evidence of the victim,
atleast, on the basic facts.
Dates of the alleged occurrence were stated totally discrepantly.
How PW1 reached the house of the appellant is not cogent.
Hence, I hold that the trial court went wrong in holding that the evidence tendered by the prosecution proved necessary the basic facts enabling the court to draw a presumption under Section 29 of the PoCSO Act.
opennyai_summary.4_October_2024__decision:
The inevitable consequence is that the appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt.
Hence, this appeal is allowed and the appellant is acquitted.
The appellant shall be released from the jail forthwith and set at liberty.
